sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Pinus palustris, the longleaf pine, is a conifer native to the southeastern United States. Mature trees commonly reach 30–37 m.

sections.title: Needles and cones
sections.text: Its exceptionally long needles, about 20–46 cm, grow in bundles of three. The heavy cones are about 15–20 cm long.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: The species is important in forestry and its needles are used as mulch. The references consulted do not establish a reliable human food use for its seeds.
